title: Janus SDK conformance case
description: One case of the SDK conformance suite (plan task 6.4, SDK spec §7, ADR 0017): a language-independent scenario every Janus SDK runs, in its own language, against a pinned engine. A case is data — the DSL usage a driver replays through its own surface, and what must come of it.

id.description: Unique case id, '<category>/<name>', matching the file's path under cases/.

category.description: translation: what a DSL chain builds, no engine. lifecycle and variants: what the SDK sends and does, against the case's own scripted engine. provider: a provider verification ('verifier', 'verify'), against the case's own scripted engine. live: against the real pinned engine, a consumer's steps or a provider's verification.

title.description: One line, in the present tense: what the SDK must do.

covers.description: The behavioural-spec conformance ids this case is the scenario for (behavioural-spec.json, a primitive's 'conformance' list).

why.description: The specification sentence this case pins, and where it is written.

note.description: What this case deliberately does not decide — an open finding, or a fact ADR 0017 places outside conformance.

janus.description: The 'janus' options this case configures beyond consumer and provider (behavioural spec 'janus'). Absent means the defaults.

components.description: The project's declared components, handed to 'janus' as its components option.

verify.description: 'provider' cases: whether the test calls 'verify' once the verifier is configured. false: it configures the verifier and its handlers and stops.

steps.description: For 'lifecycle', 'variants' and 'live': what the test does, in order.

Template.description: A value where the DSL expects a shape. Plain JSON is written as itself and compiles by the behavioural spec's 'literal' rule. An object carrying a '$' member is a shape-helper call instead: '$' is the helper's primitive id in behavioural-spec.json, 'args' its arguments in signature order, 'options' its options bag. '{ "$": "literal", "args": [ … ] }' escapes a plain object that would otherwise be read as a call.
Template.$comment: Deliberately unconstrained: a template is any JSON document, and the '$' convention is a reading of it, not a restriction on it.

$.description: A behavioural-spec shape primitive's id: 'integer', 'each-like', 'one-of', … or 'literal' to escape.

options.description: The helper's options bag, e.g. each-like's { min, max }.

MultiValue.description: A header or query value: a string, an integral number or a boolean (each written as the one string that spells it), a list of those, or a shape helper describing its one value (behavioural spec 'request'; ADR 0019). A case may also write a value the rule refuses — a fractional number, a date, null, a map — to pin that refusal, so this is deliberately unconstrained: what a value may be is the specification's rule, not this schema's.
MultiValue.$comment: Open for the same reason Template is: constraining it here would make the schema a second, quieter statement of the rule.

InteractionScript.description: A DSL chain, as data: the driver replays it through its own surface, one call per member, in this order — interaction, given*, request, response.

ScriptedEngine.description: The engine a 'lifecycle' or 'variants' case runs against: a frame pipe the driver implements, answering from this script. Every operation the SDK sends is recorded; an operation with no entry here is answered the default way (README §3).

variants.description: What 'consumer-session/variants' returns, in this order. Default: one variant, 'base'.

contract.description: The contract document 'consumer-session/finalise' returns. Absent: a small verified contract. Null is written as 'withhold-contract'.

withhold-contract.description: true: 'finalise' returns results and no contract — the engine itself withheld it.

results.description: The 'results' member of the finalise result. Default: one verified result per interaction added.

errors.description: Operation name -> the engine error that operation answers with instead (an engine-protocol §10 error document).

after.description: Answer this many calls of the operation the default way first, and error from the next one on. Absent: error from the first call.

capabilities.description: 'provider' cases: the capabilities 'engine/hello' answers with. Default: { "config-loading": {} }.

config.description: 'provider' cases: the resolved configuration 'config/load' answers with. Default: { "version": 1, "hooks": {} }.

events.description: 'provider' cases: the events the run's stream carries before its terminal one, in order; the driver numbers them. Default: one 'verification/interaction-result', { interaction: { contract: { consumer: 'web-app', provider: 'orders-api' }, index: 0, description: 'get an order' }, variant: 'base', status: 'verified' }.

summary.description: 'provider' cases: the payload of the terminal 'verification/finished' event, which carries 'last: true'. Default: { status: 'verified', variants: { verified: 1, failed: 0 } }.

invoke.description: 'provider' cases: the hooks the engine calls during the run, in order, before it answers the first 'events/poll' — each found by point and name in the 'verification/verify' frame's target.hooks, and POSTed its context at its url with its headers.

Step.description: One thing the test does. Exactly one of 'build', 'execute' or 'finalise'.

Closure.description: What the 'execute' closure does on each variant. Default: nothing, successfully.

fail-on.description: Variant ids the closure fails on — '*' for every one. It fails the way the language fails a test.

exchange.description: 'live' cases: the request the consumer sends to the mock, once per variant.

Verifier.description: The 'verifier' a provider case configures (behavioural spec 'verifier', 'state-handler', 'request-filter'), as data.

provider-url.description: The provider URL. Absent in a live case: the driver's own provider's.

pacts.description: Documents the driver writes to files, one each, and names as the 'pacts' option, in order.

config.description: A configuration file's text, which the driver writes to a file and names as 'config' by a path relative to the working directory.

transport.description: The 'transport' option, as given: the HTTP transport's drive options beside 'base-url'.

Behaviour.description: What a state handler's setup or teardown does when called, besides being recorded: return an object, throw a failure with a message, or say it cannot reach the state with a reason. Empty: return nothing.

RequestFilter.description: A request filter: it returns the request it received with each slot in 'set' replaced by the content given, or throws a failure with the message 'throws'.

set.description: Slot name -> the content the returned request has there.

MessageProducer.description: A message producer (behavioural spec 'message-producer'): it returns the message 'returns' describes, or throws a failure with the message 'throws'.

Message.description: The message a producer returns. Its body is exactly one of 'json' (a value the language holds as its own object, list, number or boolean), 'text' (a string) and 'bytes' (the language's bytes, written here as base64); 'content-type' and 'metadata' are given only when present.

authorised.description: false: the call carries no authorization header.

HandlerCall.description: One call of a declared handler, by its entry name: a state handler's 'action' ('setup' or 'teardown') and 'params', or the 'request' a request filter or a message producer received.

LiveProvider.description: The provider a live provider case's driver serves on the loopback interface. A request is answered by the first route whose method and path it has: 401 when it lacks a header 'require-headers' names, with that value, else the route's status, headers and JSON body. No route: 404.

Exchange.description: An HTTP request a 'live' case's consumer sends to the mock, written as values, not shapes.

body.description: A JSON body, sent as application/json.

closure-calls.description: The variant ids the closure ran on, in call order.

contract.description: What 'finalise' did with the contract file.

text.description: The file's exact content, including the trailing LF.

spec.description: The whole interaction-spec document the chain builds (contract.schema.json#/$defs/InteractionSpec).

at.description: JSON pointer into the built document -> the value that must be there. For a case that pins one slot of a large chain.

refused.description: true: the DSL refuses this chain at the call, before any document is built (behavioural spec 'regex', 'request'; ADR 0019). How it refuses is the language's business — a thrown error, a failed build — so the case checks only that the document was never produced.

ops.description: Every protocol operation the SDK sent, in order, across the whole case.

frames.description: Operation name -> members the SDK's request frame body must carry (a subset; members not named are not checked). The first frame of that operation.

engine-closed.description: Whether the SDK ended the engine by the end of the case (engine-protocol spec §6).

dimensions.description: 'live' cases: dimension ids the engine's selected variants must between them assign (variant semantics spec §3.9).

variant-count.description: 'live' cases: how many variants the engine must select.

outcome.description: 'provider' and live provider cases: how 'verify' ended.

result.description: 'provider' and live provider cases: the result 'verify' returned, or the one its failure carries. 'status' compared, and 'results' and 'warnings' by value when given.

warnings.description: Every 'verification/warning' payload the run's stream carried, in order (ADR 0058).

hooks.description: 'provider' cases: the 'verification/verify' frame's target.hooks, compared by value, with each url on the loopback interface written 'loopback:<path>' and each authorization header carrying a bearer token of at least 32 hex digits written 'Bearer <token>' (README §4). null: the frame has no target.hooks.

config-loaded.description: 'provider' cases: the driver handed 'config' a path relative to the working directory, and 'config/load' carried the configuration file's absolute path.

result.description: The invoke result the endpoint answered, by value; absent or null when the body was empty.

invocations.description: 'provider' cases: what the SDK's endpoint answered each of the engine's 'invoke' calls, in order.

handler-calls.description: 'provider' and live provider cases: every call of a handler the case declared, in order.

endpoint-closed.description: 'provider' cases: whether the SDK's loopback endpoint refuses connections once 'verify' has ended.

Outcome.description: How a step ended. 'ok', or the failure — a kind every language maps onto its own type (README §4).

error.description: execute-failed: the closure failed on one or more variants. contract-withheld: finalise wrote no contract. engine-error: the engine answered an operation with an error document. verification-failed: 'verify' failed because the run's status was 'failed'. refused: the SDK refused the call itself, before any frame was sent.

variants.description: execute-failed: the variant ids the failure must name.

interactions.description: contract-withheld: the interaction descriptions the failure must name.

engine-withheld.description: contract-withheld: whether the engine returned no contract (true) or the SDK withheld one it returned (false).

interaction.description: The result's interaction reference, by value, as the engine sent it.

failed.description: verification-failed: the failed, not pending, results the failure must name, in order.

ContractContent.description: A contract compared by interaction content only (ADR 0017, contract spec §5–§6): 'interactions' by description, each by its 'states', 'parts' and 'selection'. 'metadata' and the parties are never compared — they are facts about the SDK, deliberately outside content identity.
